**Finding submitted — IP: deviation (fallback target).**

- **Problem:** Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all IP therein in Licensor, and the broad "DERIVATIVE WORK" definition (p0005) captures "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements." The customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) therefore belongs entirely to Licensor, and our only right is the non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence that may not be modified or sublicensed (p0042, p0044, p0047, p0085) and dies on termination with a five-day return obligation (p0138). That fails the IP fallback.
- **What is acceptable:** Licensor's ownership of its own platform, tools and know-how is fine and left untouched; nothing assigns our IP or data to Licensor, and there is no standing Licensor licence in our data.
- **Cure:** one short inserted clause after Article III granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the customization deliverables for our business (with a targeted carve-out from the conflicting Articles II, VI and XXI mechanics), plus a confirmation that any Licensor licence in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us is limited to processing to provide the services. Fallback chosen over reversing ownership to avoid collateral rewrites.
